transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Orion CTO), Ethan Park (Orion Infra), Lena Ortiz (Orion Security), Sam Cho (Orion Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Goal: scope 4-week POC for Redwood Private deployment focusing on private networking (VPC peering / PrivateLink), region/data residency, and benchmark success criteria.
- Key success criteria discussed: latency SLOs under 200ms for 95th percentile for chat workload, throughput of ~150 concurrent sessions, data never egressing outside EU region, audit logging to customer SIEM.
- Next steps: send SOW, security docs, plan benchmarks, customer to provide VPC info.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Park: hey everyone thanks for joining we'll kick off, um, appreciate you making time. quick intros — i'm Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on this one. Jordan and Priya from SEs will handle the technical parts.
[00:08] Maya Singh: hi all, maya here. thanks. we've got Ethan, Lena and Sam on the call as well. we're trying to validate private networking and data residency for a clinician-facing assistant use case.
[00:18] Jordan Kim: great, can you give a quick rundown of the workload? average session length, tokens, qps? that kind of stuff will drive the sizing and benchmark plan.
[00:26] Sam Cho: sure — typical chat session is about 120-180 tokens per turn, usually 2-3 turns per session. peak concurrent sessions expected ~150 during clinic hours, baseline maybe 40. some batched background jobs for summarization too but lower priority.
[00:40] Ethan Park: infra constraints: we run primarily in Azure EU-West (Netherlands) region, data residency requirement is EU-only for PHI pseudonymized data; we cannot have egress to US. we prefer VNet peering or PrivateLink equivalent.
[00:53] Priya Rao: ok that helps. Redwood Private supports VPC/VNet peering and PrivateLink style endpoints — we can do peering or a managed endpoint depending on your network policy. for Azure we typically recommend private endpoint + service endpoint pattern, but peering is supported. there are tradeoffs on routing and cross-subnet egress.
[01:10] Lena Ortiz: quick security check — we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM (Splunk), SOC 2 attestation, and confirmation on KMS/HSM for key control. also, are there options to keep model weights inside the customer's VPC?
[01:22] Jordan Kim: good question. for Redwood Private the control plane is customer-managed and model artifacts live on the dedicated deployment; weights do not leave the deployment. we support customer-managed KMS integration (Azure Key Vault / HSM). audit logs can be forwarded via syslog/Splunk forwarder or pushed to an S3/GCS bucket depending on setup. we'll include specifics in the security whitepaper.
[01:40] Maya Singh: latency SLOs are important — clinicians are sensitive to lag. we want 95p latency < 200ms for small prompts and under 500ms for larger multi-turn flows. can Redwood meet that on a Private deployment?
[01:52] Jordan Kim: depends on model choice and infra. for trimmed assistant models on dedicated A10/A100-class GPUs we've seen sub-100ms token latencies for short prompts in our benchmarks; for larger context and hallucination control teams we may pick a different variant. part of the PoC is running benchmark jobs with your representative prompts. we'll scope a couple of models and quantization profiles.
[02:12] Ethan Park: on networking — we have strict egress filtering. outbound network flow to any non-EU IP must be denied. what's Redwood's recommendation for NAT/eRPC traffic for model updates or telemetry?
[02:24] Priya Rao: we can operate fully within the customer's VNet for inference traffic; management/control plane calls may need outbound to Redwood control plane unless you want an air-gapped on-prem bundle. for this POC we can do an isolated VNet peering and restrict egress with explicit allow lists. model updates can be staged via a customer-controlled storage account if you prefer.
[02:44] Sam Cho: timeline question — how long to stand up the private deployment and run benchmarks? we're aiming for a 4-week pilot with a production-like benchmark in week 3.
[02:53] Alex Park: typical timeline: week 0-1: network and onboarding (peering, certs, IAM), week 2: deployment and baseline smoke tests, week 3: benchmarks and tuning, week 4: wrap-up, quality signoff and SOW for next phase. with your team ready on VNet side we can aim for that.
[03:10] Maya Singh: ok good. cost sensitivity: we want to understand unit costs and whether dedicated capacity is required or if a smaller dedicated pool with autoscaling works.
[03:20] Jordan Kim: we'll provide cost estimates in the SOW; for predictable latency we recommend reserved/dedicated capacity. we can also demonstrate a hybrid with scaled-down dedicated nodes and fallback to hosted for non-PHI routes, but that may not meet your egress constraints.
[03:33] Lena Ortiz: for compliance, can you confirm retention policies and ability to disable logs for certain endpoints? also need SAML/SSO and RBAC.
[03:41] Priya Rao: yes — retention is configurable, and we can disable transcript persistence on a per-route basis. Redwood supports SSO (SAML/OIDC) and fine-grained RBAC; we'll include a configuration checklist in the security pack.
[03:55] Ethan Park: on the peering specifics — we use Azure VNet peering, with overlapping IP ranges avoided. we'd like to use Private Link if possible to avoid route propagation across tenants. does Redwood support Azure Private Link?
[04:07] Jordan Kim: we have a PrivateLink-style option for Azure using private endpoints; it behaves like PrivateLink where the service endpoint sits in our managed account but traffic stays on the Azure fabric. there are some extra steps for cert exchange and DNS. we'll document both peering and private endpoint flows.
[04:22] Sam Cho: benchmarking — what metrics will you capture? latency P50/P95, throughput, error rates, token cost, and also memory/cold-start times?
[04:30] Jordan Kim: yes we'll capture P50/P95/P99 latencies, throughput, tokens per second, system CPU/GPU utilization, memory/KV cache metrics, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll provide the raw logs and a summary dashboard.
[04:46] Maya Singh: for data residency we need proof that traffic and data are never routed outside EU. how do you prove that during the POC?
[04:53] Priya Rao: we can provide network diagrams, routing tables, traceroutes from the deployment, and a signed attestation for the POC. for longer-term we offer private control plane options and on-prem bundles.
[05:05] Lena Ortiz: also, we need to validate that TLS mutual auth is possible between our VNet and Redwood endpoints.
[05:10] Jordan Kim: yes mTLS is supported for service-to-service; we can provision certs or accept your PKI. we'll note that in the next steps.
[05:18] Alex Park: ok let's recap success criteria so we have alignment. Maya — can you confirm the top 3 success criteria for signoff?
[05:25] Maya Singh: sure: 1) 95p latency <200ms for clinician chat flows during peak; 2) no egress outside EU and demonstrable network proof; 3) audit logs forwarded to our Splunk and KMS controlled keys.
[05:37] Alex Park: great. Jordan — tech checklist?
[05:40] Jordan Kim: we'll run two benchmark profiles (chat interactive profile and batch summarization). we'll measure the latency and throughput targets; we'll also test private endpoint peering and validate DNS + mTLS, and export logs to your Splunk instance.
[05:55] Ethan Park: small note on DNS — if you do private endpoints we need to manage split-horizon resolution; we'll provide our DNS admins contact.
[06:02] Priya Rao: noted. we'll include DNS and cert steps in the runbook.
[06:08] Sam Cho: any blockers we should be aware of?
[06:11] Maya Singh: none yet but we need the SOW and a clear security pack to get sign-off from our InfoSec.
[06:17] Alex Park: we'll send SOW and security whitepaper. also we'll propose a 2-day benchmark window in week 3 and coordinate with Ethan on infra changes.
[06:26] Jordan Kim: for the benchmark we'll ask for a representative prompt set and a small sample dataset (anonymized) so we can reproduce clinician flows.
[06:34] Lena Ortiz: reminder — anything with PHI must be pseudonymized; we'll deliver a sanitized set.
[06:39] Alex Park: perfect. any final questions?
[06:41] Maya Singh: no, thanks everyone — looking forward to the docs and SOW.
[06:44] Alex Park: thanks all. we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule.

Call end.
